Quick notes from runtime team:
- We've reproduced the issue on a staging replica: long-running KV-cache inflation + sporadic slab fragmentation appears to trigger the GPU allocator to drop segments (reported as "tombstone" in our logs). When that happens, the inference worker returns 503s while it restarts the worker process and warms KV cache again.
- Heap/VM snapshots attached.
- Mitigation (temporary): routing affected customer traffic to an unaffected region/pool reduces p99 to normal, but increases cross-region latency ~20–40ms.

Action items:
1) Immediate: shift GreenLane's traffic to the unaffected US pool (Laura to approve and coordinate).
2) Short term: enforce smaller KV cache caps per worker to avoid runaway inflation (Rishi + runtime).
3) Long term: allocator patch to reduce fragment amplification (INF-3197).

I'll start a hotfix branch for the short-term limiter. Will post updates as we test.

Marcus
Principal Engineer, Runtime

Subject: Re: performance alert — major p99 spikes since 07:30 EDT

Update from infra/runtime team after overnight testing:
- Cause: an allocator policy regression combined with a specific request-size distribution from GreenLane caused KV-cache segment refcounts to explode. This produced persistent slab fragmentation on a subset of GPU drivers leading to an OOM-like reclaim and worker tombstoning.
- Repro: yes, deterministic on a staging mix when we replayed GreenLane traces.
- Short-term fix deployed: per-worker KV-cache soft cap + aggressive eviction (rolled at 03:40 UTC). Early telemetry shows no recurrence.
- Long-term: merged allocator patch that changes segment coalescing and introduces a periodic compaction pass (INF-3197). Target stable rollout: canary tomorrow 04:00 UTC, global next week pending metrics.

We should prepare a short technical bulletin for GreenLane: root cause, timeline, mitigation, and next steps. Marcus, can you prepare the technical appendix? Laura, I'll draft the incident timeline for execs.

Rishi
Director, Runtime Engineering

Subject: Re: performance alert — major p99 spikes since 07:30 EDT

Aisha —

Thanks again for the quick report and patience. Summary and next steps:
- What happened: our runtime's allocator + GreenLane request shape caused GPU slab fragmentation that led to worker process restarts (logged as tombstone OOMs). This briefly pushed p99 higher and produced some 503s.
- Immediate impact mitigation: we rerouted GreenLane traffic to an unaffected pool within ~10 minutes; your checkout failures should have stopped then.
- Short-term fix: per-worker KV-cache cap + eviction (deployed 03:40 UTC) — no recurrence in 24h.
- Long-term fix & timeline: allocator compaction merged (INF-3197). Canary 04:00 UTC tomorrow, planned rollout globally next week.
- What we will deliver: a post-incident report by Monday EOD including heap dumps, traces, a technical appendix, and the canary results. We will also schedule a 30-minute tech sync with your SREs — proposed Tuesday 10:00 EDT.

Please tell us if Tuesday works and whether you need any further artifacts sooner (we can share the heap dump and traces now under an SRE-only folder).
